q: 1. The weight per unit volume of a liquid at a standard temperature and pressure is called
explain: Specific weight (w or γ) represents the force exerted by gravity on a unit volume of a fluid.

q: 2. The specific weight of water in S.I. units is taken as
explain: All these values are equivalent: 9.81 kN/m³ = 9810 N/m³. Converting to mm³, it becomes 9.81 x 10⁻⁶ N/mm³.

q: 3. The specific gravity of an oil whose specific weight is 7.85 kN/m³, is
explain: Specific Gravity = Specific weight of oil / Specific weight of water = 7.85 / 9.81 ≈ 0.8.

q: 4. The unit of surface tension is
explain: As it represents the force acting along a line on the surface, its SI unit is Newtons per metre (N/m).

q: 5. The pressure less than atmospheric pressure is known as
explain: All these terms describe pressures below the local atmospheric level.

q: 6. The pressure of a liquid measured with the help of a piezometer tube is
explain: A piezometer measures the pressure head relative to the atmosphere, thus providing gauge pressure.

q: 7. The total pressure on a horizontally immersed surface is
explain: Total pressure (P) = specific weight (w) * Area (A) * depth of centroid (x̄).

q: 8. The total pressure on an immersed surface inclined at an angle θ with the liquid surface is
explain: Total pressure is independent of the angle of inclination and depends only on the area and the depth of the centroid.

q: 9. The depth of centre of pressure for an immersed surface inclined at an angle θ with the liquid surface lies at a distance equal to _________ the centre of gravity.
explain: For inclined surfaces, the vertical distance below the centroid is adjusted by the sin² θ component.

q: 10. A vertical wall is subjected to a pressure due to one kind of liquid, on one of its sides. The total pressure on the wall acts at a distance _________ from the liquid surface.
explain: The centre of pressure for a rectangular vertical surface is at 2/3 of the depth from the top (free surface).

q: 11. The centre of gravity of the volume of the liquid displaced is called
explain: The buoyant force acts through the centroid of the displaced volume, known as the Centre of Buoyancy.

q: 12. When a liquid is flowing through a pipe, the velocity of the liquid is
options: maximum at the centre and minimum near the walls
minimum at the centre and maximum near the walls
zero at the centre and maximum near the walls
maximum at the centre and zero near the walls
explain: Due to viscosity and the 'no-slip condition' at the boundaries, velocity is zero at the walls and reaches its peak at the pipe's centerline.

q: 13. A flow in which the quantity of liquid flowing per second is not constant, is called
explain: Unsteady flow occurs when parameters at a point vary over time.

q: 14. When a cylindrical vessel, containing some liquid, is rotated about its vertical axis, the liquid surface is depressed down at the axis of its rotation and rises up near the walls of the vessel on all sides. This type of flow is known as ............
explain: Vortex flow is the motion of a fluid in a curved path or around a central axis. This specific case is a 'forced vortex'.

q: 15. According to Newton's law of viscosity, the shear stress on a layer of a fluid is ............ to the rate of shear strain.
explain: Newton's law states that $\tau = \mu (du/dy)$, where shear stress is directly proportional to the velocity gradient (rate of shear strain).

q: 16. A flow in which the viscosity of fluid is dominating over the inertia force is called ............
explain: Laminar flow occurs at low velocities where viscous forces are strong enough to keep fluid particles in smooth layers.

q: 17. The celerity (velocity) of a pressure wave in a fluid is given by ...............
explain: The speed of sound (celerity) in a fluid depends on its elasticity (Bulk modulus K) and its inertia (Density ρ), calculated as √(K/ρ).

q: 18. Whenever a plate is held immersed at some angle with the direction of flow of the liquid, it is subjected to some pressure. The component of this pressure, in the direction of flow of the liquid, is known as ...............
explain: The force component acting parallel to the direction of motion is 'drag', while the component perpendicular to the motion is 'lift'.

q: 19. The product of mass and acceleration of flowing liquid is called ...............
explain: In accordance with Newton's second law, F = ma, where the product of mass and acceleration represents the inertia force.

q: 20. To avoid the force of surface tension in an inclined manometer, the minimum angle of inclination is ...............
explain: Standard practice in fluid mechanics suggests a minimum angle of 4 degrees to minimize the inaccuracies caused by surface tension/capillarity.

q: 21. An ideal flow of a liquid obeys ...............
explain: All fluid flows, including ideal (non-viscous, incompressible) flows, must satisfy the principle of conservation of mass, represented by the continuity equation.

q: 22. The dimensionless parameter not applicable to flowing liquids, is ...............
explain: Kinematic viscosity (ν) has units of m²/s; it is a physical property, not a dimensionless parameter.

q: 23. Hydraulic ram is a device ...............
options: for lifting water without an electric motor
explain: A hydraulic ram uses the energy of a large quantity of water falling through a small height to lift a small quantity of water to a much greater height without external power.

q: 24. The intensity of pressure due to sudden closure of a valve... is directly proportional to ...............
options: square root of the bulk modulus
explain: The pressure rise ($p$) due to water hammer is given by $p = ho v C$, where the wave velocity $C$ is $\sqrt{K/ho}$. Thus, pressure is proportional to $\sqrt{K}$ (square root of bulk modulus).

q: 25. The equation τ = μ (dv/dy) for the viscosity, is suggested ...............
explain: This is Newton's Law of Viscosity, where shear stress is proportional to the rate of shear strain (velocity gradient).

q: 26. Kinematic viscosity is defined as equal to ...............
explain:
Kinematic viscosity ($
u$) represents the ratio of dynamic viscosity ($\mu$) to the fluid density ($ho$): $
u = \mu / ho$.

q: 27. Stoke is the unit of ...............
explain: Stoke is the CGS unit of kinematic viscosity ($1 Stoke = 1 cm^2/s$).

q: 28. The multiplying factor for converting one poise into M.K.S. unit of dynamic viscosity is ...............
explain: In the M.K.S system ($kgf \cdot s / m^2$), 1 poise is equivalent to roughly 0.01019 units, but the standard SI conversion is $1 Poise = 0.1 N \cdot s/m^2$. The closest M.K.S factor logic leads to 0.981/10.

q: 29. Surface tension has the units of ...............
explain: Surface tension is the force acting across an imaginary line on the liquid surface, expressed as Force/Length ($N/m$).

q: 30. Centre of pressure of a plane surface immersed in a liquid is ...............
explain: Because hydrostatic pressure increases with depth, the lower half of an immersed surface experiences more force, shifting the resultant force (centre of pressure) below the geometric center (CG).

q: 31. For submerged curved surface, the vertical component of the hydrostatic force is ...............
explain: The vertical component of force on a curved surface is equal to the weight of the liquid contained in the volume vertically above the curved surface up to the free surface.

q: 32. When the fluid is at rest, the shear stress is ...............
explain: Shear stress requires a velocity gradient (flow). In a static fluid, there is no relative motion between layers, so shear stress is zero.

q: 33. The meacentric height of a floating body is ...............
options: distance between metacentre and centre of buoyancy
distance between centre of buoyancy and centre of gravity
distance between metacentre and centre of gravity
explain: Metacentric height ($GM$) is the vertical distance between the centre of gravity ($G$) and the metacentre ($M$).

q: 34. For a submerged body, if the centre of buoyancy coincides with the centre of gravity, the equilibrium is called
explain: When the center of gravity (G) and the center of buoyancy (B) coincide, the body remains in its new position after being disturbed, which defines neutral equilibrium.

q: 35. If the density of a fluid changes from point to point in a flow region, it is called
explain: Compressible flow is a flow where the density of the fluid changes from point to point, usually due to changes in pressure.

q: 36. Study of fluid at rest, is known as
explain: Fluid Statics (Hydrostatics) is the study of fluids that are not in motion.

q: 37. For a sub-merged curved surface, the horizontal component of force due to static liquid is equal to
options: weight to liquid supported by the curved surface
force on a projection of the curved surface on a vertical plane
area of curved surface × pressure at the centroid
explain: The horizontal component of hydrostatic force on a curved surface is equal to the force exerted on the vertical projection of that curved surface.

q: 38. Euler's number is the ratio of
explain: Euler's number (Eu) expresses the relationship between the inertia force and the pressure force in a fluid flow.

q: 39. The square root of the ratio of inertia force to force due to compressibility is known as
explain: The Mach number is the square root of the ratio of the inertia force to the force due to compressibility (elastic force).

q: 40. Total drag on a body is the sum of
explain: Total drag consists of skin friction drag (viscous resistance) and pressure drag (form drag due to pressure differences between the front and back of the body).

q: 41. When a falling body has attained terminal velocity, the weight of the body is equal to
options: drag force plus the buoyant force
explain: At equilibrium (terminal velocity), the downward Weight (W) is balanced by the upward forces: Drag (Fd) and Buoyancy (Fb). Thus, W = Fd + Fb.

q: 42. The boundary layer is called turbulent boundary layer if
explain: For flow over a flat plate, the transition from laminar to turbulent boundary layer typically occurs at a critical Reynolds number of approximately 5 × 10⁵.

q: 43. Super-sonic flow means
explain: Supersonic flow is defined as flow where the speed of the fluid exceeds the local speed of sound, resulting in a Mach number greater than 1.

q: 44. Sonic-flow means
explain: Sonic flow occurs when the fluid velocity is exactly equal to the local speed of sound (Mach = 1).

q: 45. In super-sonic flow, the projectile (which creates disturbances) moves
explain: In supersonic flow, the projectile travels faster than the speed of sound (the speed of disturbances), so it stays ahead of the pressure waves it creates.

q: 46. For a supersonic flow, velocity increases
options: with the decrease of area of flow
with the increase of area of flow
when area of flow is constant
explain: As noted in question 495, for supersonic flow (Mach > 1), the velocity increases as the cross-sectional area of flow increases.
